rationale: This is a mechanical leg-addition to the archive's winning MIN construct whose profitability leg was already tested in WeakestLinkProfitSolvency, and the three-way minimum of ranks predictably concentrates on whichever leg is noisiest, so it offers an attribution footnote rather than a new mechanism and its hypothesis ("the market prices the average") is not identified by the expression.

By its own admission this is a smoothing robustness check on the archive leader with legs and combiner held fixed, and the persistence dimension was already probed by StressTestedFixedClaimCoverage's five-year TS_MIN, making it the cosmetic-variant case the objective explicitly warns against.

The level-plus-direction complementarity is a genuinely new combiner for this archive, but deflating liabilities by gross profit without a positivity screen makes lt/(revt−cogs) flip sign for negative-gross-profit firms, so NEG() assigns the worst-off firms top "low burden" ranks — an internal inconsistency with the hypothesis that also contaminates the DELTA leg.

Because xint/lt is small and highly persistent, this is dominated by ΔROA — the well-documented profitability-change/earnings-momentum predictor — and the hypothesis about *crossing* the zero-spread boundary is not what a continuous first difference computes.

The expression is just EBITDA-to-assets plus negative-net-debt-to-assets with arbitrary unit weights, i.e. an unweighted sum of two separately published anomalies (profitability, cash/leverage) and a close cousin of the archive's EbitdaPlusCashRunway, so it tests linearity at the cost of proposing no new economics.

Substituting working-capital-over-liabilities for cash-over-current-liabilities keeps the economic role of the liquidity leg while stripping out the published cash-holdings content, making this a well-posed and cheap attribution test that changes the signal's information content rather than merely its parameterization.
